topics.title: Macroeconomic Stability, Balance-of-Payments, and Structural Reforms
topics.summary: Pakistan's economic trajectory focused on fiscal discipline, broadening the tax net, containing inflation, restructuring state-owned enterprises, and securing sustained external sector financing.
key_facts: Primary causes of balance-of-payments crises: Chronic trade deficit due to low-value-added exports, heavy reliance on imported energy and machinery, low domestic tax-to-GDP ratio (~9-10%), and heavy external debt servicing.

Key structural reforms: Broadening tax net through FBR digitalization (Tajir Dost scheme), curbing undocumented retail, rationalizing power tariffs to address circular debt, and privatizing loss-making SOEs (e.g. PIA, DISCOs).
Inflation and Monetary Policy: State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) policy rate recalibration based on headline CPI inflation trends, targeting single-digit inflation.
Foreign Exchange Reserves: Sustained through bilateral deposits (China, Saudi Arabia, UAE), IMF Extended Fund Facility (EFF) disbursements, and worker remittances exceeding $30 billion annually.
potential_interview_questions: What is the primary cause of Pakistan's recurring balance-of-payments challenges?
What are two structural reforms required to resolve Pakistan's economic crisis permanently?
Why is export competitiveness more sustainable than relying on external loans or remittances?

topics.title: Special Investment Facilitation Council (SIFC) and Economic Revival
topics.summary: Civil-military apex body established to act as a single-window facilitator for foreign direct investment (FDI) across strategic sectors.
key_facts: Established in June 2023 with a hybrid civil-military leadership structure to eliminate bureaucratic delays.

Five Priority Focus Sectors: Agriculture & Livestock (corporate farming initiatives), Information Technology (IT exports and tech parks), Mines & Minerals (Reko Diq copper-gold project), Energy & Power (renewables, transmission overhaul), and Tourism.
Key Projects: Reko Diq mining agreements with Barrick Gold, Green Pakistan Initiative (GPI) for smart agriculture, and bilateral investment treaties with Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states.
potential_interview_questions: What is the mandate of the SIFC and which priority sectors does it target?
How can the Reko Diq project transform Pakistan's mining and foreign exchange earnings?
What role does agricultural modernization play in food security and import substitution?

topics.title: China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) Phase 2 and Regional Connectivity
topics.summary: Transitioning from early-harvest energy and infrastructure projects to industrial cooperation, Special Economic Zones (SEZs), agriculture, and business-to-business (B2B) joint ventures.
key_facts: CPEC Phase 1 completed major highways (Karakoram Highway upgrade, Sukkur-Multan Motorway), coal and hydro power plants, and early Gwadar Port infrastructure.
CPEC Phase 2 Focus: Five Corridors of Growth: Growth Corridor, Livelihood Corridor, Innovation Corridor, Green Corridor, and Open/Inclusive Corridor.
Priority SEZs: Rashakai SEZ (KPK), Dhabeji SEZ (Sindh), Allama Iqbal Industrial City (Punjab), and Boston SEZ (Balochistan).
Gwadar Strategic Role: Deep-sea port offering China shortest overland access to Arabian Sea; Gwadar International Airport commissioned to integrate logistics.
potential_interview_questions: How does CPEC Phase 2 differ fundamentally from Phase 1?
What is the geoeconomic significance of Gwadar Port for Pakistan and landlocked Central Asian Republics?
How can Special Economic Zones boost domestic industrial productivity?
